baseline.text: Sonra size onlara karşı yeniden üstünlük verdik, sizi mallar ve oğullarla destekledik ve sayınızı daha çok yaptık.

findings.text: Yeniden üstünlük, mal ve oğulların birbirine eklenen desteğiyle topluluğun tekrar toplanıp harekete geçebilmesini sağlayan bir kapasite inşasıdır.
İleride desteğin iki karşıt yola da verildiğinin açıklanması, buradaki maddi artışın tek başına ayrıcalıklı kabulün kanıtı olmadığını gösterir.

activation_trace.role: Return to a former position supplies restoration as the first motion of the reversal.
A renewed charge after withdrawal turns restored position into regained initiative against them.

changed_reading.after: The clause stages a directional reversal: lost initiative is restored as a renewed countercharge.
changed_reading.before: A turn against the opposing group was given back.

baseline_models.mechanism: The paired motions of returning and renewed attack reverse direction: a lost initiative is restored as an active counterturn against the former aggressors.

activation_trace.role: A connected increase that supplies aid makes wealth and sons inputs to a larger capacity.
Accumulated property supplies the durable material base of the restored capacity.
Sonship and descent supply generational continuity and an enlarging kin body.
Prevailing through number converts added resources and descendants into comparative strength.
A rallying and supporting group is the social output in which the preceding additions become operative.

changed_reading.after: Recovery is engineered as the conversion of durable resources and lineage into a larger ready-to-rally coalition.
changed_reading.before: They received wealth, sons, and more manpower.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَأَمْدَدْنَٰكُم بِأَمْوَٰلٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا
baseline_models.mechanism: Connected additions are converted into mobilizable capacity: stored wealth sustains action, sons continue and enlarge the social body, and the result is numerical superiority in a group ready to rally.

activation_trace.role: Sonship anchors the focus addition in descent and generational continuation.
The earlier occurrence identifies the addressed collective through descent, giving the focus sons a corporate lineage.
Gentle direction toward a path makes inherited continuity answerable to guidance rather than valuable by number alone.
The carrying of a visible burden supplies preservation through passage as the ancestry behind renewed continuity.

changed_reading.after: Sons mark restored intergenerational continuity, renewing a guided and accountable historical collective as well as its numbers.
changed_reading.before: Sons are one input to increased manpower.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same descent root first names a people addressed through guidance, while the next ayah places their ancestry among descendants carried through an earlier rescue. The focus sons therefore renew a transmitted historical body, not merely a pool of recruits.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies descent, guidance, and an ancestral carrying; I infer that renewed sons carry forward a historically obligated body. A live alternative is the narrower demographic reading in which sons simply enlarge military support.
structural_cues: The sequence moves from children of Israel, to descendants carried with Noah, to the focus gift of sons.

activation_trace.role: Return to a former position supplies recovery after the preceding displacement.
Renewed attack supplies the outward counter-motion that follows recovered position.
A temporally repeated occurrence places the focus reversal inside a counted sequence rather than an isolated battle.
Movement back and forth within dwellings supplies the depth of the prior incursion that the focus reverses.
Gaps between things provide the penetrated pathways, making the defeat an interior breach rather than pressure at a boundary.

changed_reading.after: The focus is the hinge that reverses an interior occupation into recovered outward initiative within the first counted cycle.
changed_reading.before: The focus restores initiative in general.

context_deltas.mechanism: A counted recurrence is followed by hostile movement through the gaps and interiors of the dwellings. The focus counterturn answers that penetration by reversing the vector of force, so restoration is specifically recovery from an internal breach.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies counted recurrence and hostile traversal through interior gaps; I infer that the focus return reverses that spatial and political vector. The live alternative is recovery of power without a literal counter-invasion.
structural_cues: The adjacent directional phrase changes from forces sent against you in 17:5 to the restored turn against them in 17:6.

activation_trace.role: Return after withdrawal anchors the restored turn while retaining the possibility of another reversal.
Destruction, invalidation, and breaking supply the later endpoint that prevents the focus recovery from reading as final.
Merciful tenderness keeps the post-restoration future open rather than mechanically fixed.
Matched return after departure supplies the explicit feedback rule governing any renewed conduct.

changed_reading.after: The counterturn is a contingent respite inside a recursive moral-historical cycle whose direction can reverse again.
changed_reading.before: The restored counterturn resolves the preceding defeat.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next movement forecasts another destructive entry, then holds mercy beside a matched return: if the addressed group resumes, the divine response resumes. The focus restoration is thus a reversible interval in a feedback cycle, not a terminal victory.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a second destructive horizon, mercy, and the matched conditional return; I infer that conduct controls which direction the cycle takes. A live alternative is to read 17:6 simply as one historical respite without a general feedback model.
structural_cues: The later promise in 17:7 mirrors the first promise before the focus, and 17:8 states its return relation conditionally.

activation_trace.role: Accumulated property represents a transferable collective resource.
The rallying group embodies the collective capacity that the later accounting refuses to treat as one moral person.
Binding a judgment to its bearer supplies the personal attachment that counters fungible group strength.
The person's own self supplies the irreducible unit of reckoning.
Counting and account turn responsibility into an individually inspectable ledger.
A heavy burden supplies the liability that one bearer cannot shift onto descendants or coalition.

changed_reading.after: The verse inventories transferable worldly capacity while the later context sharply withholds transferability from moral responsibility.
changed_reading.before: The larger coalition may appear to certify the restored collective.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus assembles collective assets, but the later sequence attaches a record to each person, makes the self sufficient as reckoner, and denies transfer of another's burden. Mobilizable power is collective and fungible; moral liability is personal and nonfungible.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies personal attachment, self-accounting, and non-carriage of another's burden; I infer that plural assets cannot convert into moral credit or discharge. The live alternative is that those assets still acquire ethical value through how individuals use them.
structural_cues: The plural recipients and collective increase of 17:6 give way to each human, your book, your self, and no bearer in 17:13-15.

activation_trace.role: Connected increase supplies the focus wealth and sons as effective aid.
Numerical prevalence anchors the worldly comparative whose ultimate significance is revised.
Acceleration and bringing forward mark the immediate horizon within which worldly reinforcement can be desired.
The repeated extension broadens the focus mechanism from one restored group to both contrasted recipient classes.
Handing over a gift identifies the supply as a grant rather than evidence of the recipient's intrinsic merit.
The absence of withholding makes extension available across the moral contrast and blocks endorsement by possession alone.
Degrees of excellence relocate the decisive comparison beyond the focus advantage in manpower.

changed_reading.after: They are genuine but provisional capacities within a giving extended across opposed orientations, and their comparative rank is not ultimate.
changed_reading.before: Wealth, sons, and superior manpower can sound like proof that the restored group is approved.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context places immediate-world pursuit beside an extension granted to both contrasted groups, calls that grant an unrestricted giving, and reserves larger degrees of excellence for the hereafter. The focus endowment is real power but not a moral certificate or ultimate rank.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate pursuit, extension to both sides, unrestricted giving, and a greater later hierarchy; I infer that provision grants capacity without certifying moral standing. A live alternative is that the particular restoration in 17:6 still functions as a specific mercy or strategic favor.
structural_cues: In 17:20 both these and those receive extension, while 17:21 explicitly contrasts worldly differentiation with greater hereafter degrees.

remaining_uncertainties: The final rallying noun may emphasize an actively mobilized force, a wider supporting kin group, or both.
The sons can remain primarily demographic support even though the lineage sequence activates inherited continuity and obligation.
The directional reversal is clear, but its degree of literal military counter-invasion remains open.
strongest_changes: The immediate sequence turns generic restoration into a vector reversal after interior breach and then into one phase of a conditional recurring cycle.
The personal ledger of 17:13-15 prevents collective wealth, descendants, or manpower from transferring moral liability or becoming moral credit.
The repeated extension to both groups in 17:20 detaches provision from endorsement, while 17:21 relativizes the focus comparative against a greater hierarchy.
summary.what_was_special: The focus densely converts return into reinforcement and reinforcement into mobilizable plurality. Context changes chiefly the temporal and moral status of that power, while the aligned water branches across return, turn, and extension preserve an unusual replenishment model as a contained analogy.

activation_trace.role: Stored fullness and accumulated water supply the first image of a depleted capacity being recharged.
Collected water in a pool turns the restored turn into a reservoir of recovered initiative.
One flow replenishing another converts the reservoir image into continuing supply through wealth and sons.
The rallying group keeps the hydraulic analogy attached to its actual social and mobilizational endpoint.

changed_reading.after: Restoration behaves like hydraulic recharge: pooled capacity is replenished into wealth, descendants, and a larger rallying mass.
changed_reading.before: Aid adds a static stock of assets and people.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it aligns three water-related, form-distant branch images across consecutive focus roots; it remains anchored in the ordered return-turn-extension chain and reaches the explicit social result. Downstream prose should label it a material analogy for replenishment, not claim that the focus words lexically mean a water system.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Restoration is a supplied capacity to remuster.** `ر د د:B001` returns what was sent away, `ك ر ر:B001/B008` joins renewed turn with a gathered troop, `م د د:B002` supplies connected increase, and `ن ف ر:B002/B003` musters a supporting band. Wealth and sons are inserted between returned turn and enlarged muster. I infer material and relational extension → renewed collective capacity. The ayah reads restoration as rebuilt mobilization infrastructure rather than a bare reversal of fortunes.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:20 and 17:70 broaden extension, provision, and carriage beyond this factional restoration. The later universal frame corrected any reading of material increase as proof of exclusive favor.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Restoration as replenishing a mobilizable body.** Lexical evidence: `م د د B002` (connected increase that supplies another), `ك ر ر B008` (gathered company or troop), and `ن ف ر B002` (mustering and going forth to aid or war) in `أَمْدَدْنَٰكُم`, `ٱلْكَرَّةَ`, and `نَفِيرًا`. Structural cue: reversal is followed in sequence by wealth, sons, and increased `نفير`, between the two incursions of 17:5 and 17:7. Assigned role: extension replenishes inputs, `الكرة` regathers them, and `نفير` converts them into collective capacity. Abductive move: the ayah lists the inputs and the larger muster; I infer that supply enables remobilization. Reading change: the restoration is a rebuilt social logistics system, not three disconnected gifts.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:7 made `نَفِيرًا` operational: the restored wealth and sons in 17:6 are inputs into a body that can again enter collective conflict, not an inert abundance list.

words.gloss_range: delayed sequencing particle opening a new restoration phase after the prior punishment scene
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) opens the ayah as a delayed sequel after the punishment scene of 17:5. Its first position sets the frame for all three following divine acts: the turn is returned, the addressees are reinforced, and they are finally made greater in mobilized force. The fixed particle form carries no participant marking, but the doubled sound makes the temporal break feel weighty before restoration begins.

topics.headline: delayed sequel after punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that restoration begins after an interval from 17:5, not as an immediate continuation of the punishment scene.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as temporal sequencing with delay, and its opening position scopes over the following restoration clauses.

topics.headline: three-act restoration architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the delayed opening governs a sequence of strategic reversal, material reinforcement, and mobilized capacity.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence separates three coordinated verbal clauses, matching the CRITICAL architecture row.

topics.headline: fixed form and doubled sound mark the break
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector is formally compact but audibly weighted, so the boundary feels like a real pause before restoration.
topics.reason: The particle has no inflectional participants, while its geminated sound supports the delayed boundary already licensed by grammar.

words.gloss_range: completed divine returning/restoring action with object, beneficiary, and adversarial complement
words.prose: {{ar:رَدَدْنَا}} ({{tr:radadnā}}) states the first restoration act as completed divine action. In one compact frame it governs the returned turn, the beneficiaries, and the adversarial party, so the grammar itself maps reversal: for the addressees and against the prior attackers. The root field contributes return, reversal, and answer-back pressure, while the Form I transitive verb keeps the action as divine restoration rather than the group turning back by itself.
words.root_gloss_range: returning, restoring, rejecting, and reversing; local syntax selects restored reversal

topics.headline: completed divine return opens the verb chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first restoration act is asserted as completed divine action and sets the aspect for the later verbs.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person plural form supports completed divine agency and begins the three-verb chain.

topics.headline: one verb maps object, beneficiary, and adversary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar itself draws a reversal map: the turn, the beneficiary, and the defeated side are all governed by one verb.
topics.reason: The attachment frame confirms the object, benefactive phrase, and adversarial phrase under the same verb.

topics.headline: return field narrowed to restored reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root image of return and answer-back pressure, while local syntax keeps the sense to a worldly restored turn.
topics.reason: The broader root includes return, rejection, and answer/refutation; the local object and adversarial phrase narrow it to restored reversal.

topics.headline: Form I keeps God as restoring agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the action is not reflexive reversion by the group but transitive restoration performed by the divine speaker.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb with first-person plural subject contrasts with reflexive reversion patterns without making those patterns govern the verse.

topics.headline: worldly return distinguished from cosmic return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this return belongs to historical restoration, even though the same root can mark return to God in 6:62 and 10:30.
topics.reason: The intertext rows give concrete return-to-God contrasts, while local complements keep 17:6 in a worldly dominance frame.

words.gloss_range: dative-benefactive preposition plus second-person plural suffix marking the addressed beneficiaries
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمُ}} ({{tr:lakumu}}) makes the addressees explicit beneficiaries before the returned object is even named. The lām phrase says the turn is for them, while the suffix keeps Banī Isrāʾīl in view from the previous address. Set beside {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}), it creates the compact polarity of for-you versus against-them.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the adversarial phrase paired with the beneficiary phrase

topics.headline: for-you beneficiary is explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the restored turn is explicitly for the already-addressed group, not merely moving back in abstract space.
topics.reason: The lām phrase is attached as recipient complement, and the suffix preserves the prior addressee chain.

topics.headline: beneficiary versus adversary polarity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the zero-sum axis: one side receives the turn and the other side has it fall against them.
topics.reason: The opposed prepositional phrases are both licensed under the return frame.

topics.headline: recipient foregrounded before the returned turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the beneficiary is named before the object, making the recipient relation land before the turn itself is specified.
topics.reason: The local word order and liaison vowel support foregrounding without changing the core benefactive syntax.

words.gloss_range: definite single-instance turn returned as the object of the verb, with adversarial charge coloring
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكَرَّةَ}} ({{tr:al-karrata}}) is the definite, accusative object of the returning verb: the identifiable turn itself is what is restored. Its single-instance shape bounds the restoration as one episode in the larger 17:4-8 cycle, while the following adversarial phrase lets the word carry a battle-turn overtone. The karra field also contrasts wished or losing returns in 2:167, 26:102, 39:58, and 79:12 with a granted worldly return here.
words.root_gloss_range: return, recurrence, and charge-back imagery; local grammar selects a granted restored turn

topics.headline: the identifiable bounded turn is the object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is returned is the identifiable turn itself, bounded as one occurrence within the cycle.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence confirm the word as a definite accusative direct object and single-instance noun.

topics.headline: return becomes an adversarial turn of force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the battle-turn overtone: the returned turn is not neutral recurrence but momentum back against the prior attackers.
topics.reason: The object is governed by the return verb and followed by the adversarial phrase, so charge imagery is retained as coloring, not made the sole gloss.

topics.headline: granted return contrasts failed wished returns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is a granted worldly return, unlike wished or losing returns in 2:167, 26:102, 39:58, and 79:12.
topics.reason: The cited karra field supports contrast, while the local definite object keeps 17:6 specific and historical.

words.gloss_range: prepositional phrase marking the adversarial party over or against whom the turn operates
